stated: Reform UK will improve HMRC's competence to collect tens of billions in unpaid taxes, which they attribute to understaffing and bad management.

source.quote: Collect £ Billions in Unpaid Tax HM Revenue and Customs failed to collect tens of billions in taxes last year due to understaffing and bad management. Improved HMRC competence would deliver lower taxes to British workers.

bearing_set.reason: Collecting tens of billions in currently unpaid taxes directly increases government revenue without new borrowing or rate rises, improving the funded/borrowed balance and debt-path sustainability.

The UK tax gap is disproportionately driven by complex avoidance and evasion concentrated among higher-earning individuals and businesses; stronger enforcement would likely narrow the income/wealth gap by making those with greatest capacity to avoid pay what is owed.

membership_note: The policy does not change tax rates (so O11 is not in scope for compliant taxpayers), and any downstream prosperity or public-service effects depend on how additional revenue is deployed — not on this policy itself. O10 (surveillance/coercion) is not clearly triggered since the stated mechanism is staffing and management reform rather than new enforcement powers.
